policy.title: Analytic Standards
policy.purpose: Establishes five core Analytic Standards and nine Analytic Tradecraft Standards that govern the production and evaluation of all IC analytic products. Every analytic product shall be consistent with these standards.

rule.name: Objective
rule.text: Analysts must perform their functions with objectivity and with awareness of their own assumptions and reasoning. Employ reasoning techniques that reveal and mitigate bias. Consider alternative perspectives and contrary information. Do not be unduly constrained by previous judgments when new developments indicate a modification is necessary.

rule.name: Independent of political consideration
rule.text: Analytic assessments must not be distorted by, nor shaped for, advocacy of a particular audience, agenda, or policy viewpoint. Analytic judgments must not be influenced by preference for a particular policy.

rule.name: Timely
rule.text: Analysis must be disseminated in time to be actionable by customers. Remain aware of events of intelligence interest, customer activities, and intelligence priorities.

rule.name: Based on all available sources
rule.text: Analysis should be informed by all relevant information available. Identify and address critical information gaps.

rule.name: Implements tradecraft standards
rule.text: Analytic products must implement the nine Analytic Tradecraft Standards listed in the next section.

rule.name: Sources quality and credibility
rule.text: Identify underlying sources and methodologies upon which judgments are based. Use source descriptors to describe factors affecting source quality and credibility: accuracy and completeness, possible denial and deception, age and currency, technical elements of collection, source access, validation, motivation, possible bias, and expertise. Source summary statements are strongly encouraged.

rule.name: Expresses uncertainty
rule.text:
Indicate and explain the basis for uncertainties associated with major judgments: the likelihood of an event and the analyst's confidence in the basis for that judgment. Note causes of uncertainty and explain how they affect analysis. Identify indicators that would alter the level of uncertainty.
When expressing likelihood, use exactly one of the two term-sets defined in the probability scale below. Do not mix terms from different rows without a disclaimer noting they refer to the same probability.
Do not combine a confidence level (such as "high confidence") with a degree of likelihood in the same sentence.

rule.name: Distinguishes information from judgment
rule.text: Clearly separate statements conveying underlying intelligence information from statements conveying assumptions or judgments. State assumptions explicitly when they serve as the linchpin of an argument or bridge information gaps. Explain the implications for judgments if assumptions prove incorrect. Identify indicators that, if detected, would alter judgments.

definition.meaning: A supposition used to frame or support an argument.
A conclusion based on underlying intelligence information, analysis, and assumptions.

rule.name: Analysis of alternatives
rule.text: Systematically evaluate differing hypotheses to explain events, explore near-term outcomes, and imagine possible futures. Identify and assess plausible alternative hypotheses, particularly when judgments contend with significant uncertainty or when low-probability events could produce high-impact results. Address associated assumptions, likelihood, and implications. Identify indicators that would affect the likelihood of alternatives.

rule.name: Customer relevance
rule.text: Provide information and insight on issues relevant to customers. Address implications: prospects, context, threats, or factors affecting opportunities for action.

rule.name: Clear argumentation
rule.text: Present a clear main analytic message up front. A multi-judgment product must have an overall message drawn from those judgments. Support all judgments with relevant intelligence and coherent reasoning. Language and syntax should convey meaning unambiguously. Be internally consistent and acknowledge significant supporting and contrary information.

rule.name: Change or consistency
rule.text: State how major judgments are consistent with, differ from, or represent initial coverage relative to previously published analysis. Avoid boilerplate; make clear how new information or reasoning led to the current judgments. Recurrent products should note any changes; when there are no changes, they need not confirm consistency. Significant differences between IC elements should be brought to customers' attention.

rule.name: Accurate judgments
rule.text: Apply expertise and logic to make the most accurate judgments possible, based on available information and known gaps. Do not avoid difficult judgments to minimise the risk of being wrong. Express judgments as clearly and precisely as possible, addressing likelihood, timing, and nature of the outcome.

rule.name: Visual information
rule.text: Use visuals to clarify an analytic message and to complement or enhance the presentation of data and analysis, particularly for spatial or temporal relationships. Visuals must be clear and pertinent; analytic content in visuals must adhere to other tradecraft standards.
